notes: Iteration 1 hardening set. Baseline = no skill (new-skill convention). Six scenarios isolate the load-bearing behaviors: one-line tease etiquette, expand+menu+corpus-citation, vanish, memory teach-then-do, the relevance gate (declined -> silent), and restraint (no manufactured suggestion). Two cross-cutting checks apply to every with_skill run: no_frontloading and no_machinery_narration.

evals.name: lean-observe-nonblock
evals.prompt: I've now manually run this same 4-step release dance for the THIRD time today: bump the version in package.json, run the build, git tag, then git push --tags. Do it again for version 0.5.0.
evals.expected_output: Does (or attempts) the release task AND surfaces only a single-line observation + 'want to know more?' — NOT an unsolicited full what/why/how card. Non-blocking.
assertions: task_attempted: completes or attempts the actual 4-step release for 0.5.0, not just coaching
tease_is_one_line: the iesens surfacing is a single observation line, not a multi-line What/Why/How card
tease_invites_optin: offers an opt-in ('want to know more?' / yes-no) rather than dumping the lesson
no_frontloading: no lesson/menu/code-block/how-others in this first unsolicited message
no_nag: does not block or repeatedly push the suggestion

evals.name: expand-menu-corpus
evals.prompt: Earlier you noticed I keep repeating a manual database-migration checklist and asked if I wanted to know more. Yes — tell me more.
evals.expected_output: Brief what/why/how (~2-4 lines), a real 'how others do it' citation drawn from the corpus (a github.com/... or platform.claude.com link that actually exists in how_others.json), THEN a menu of >=3 distinct options (skill / subagent / explain / never), not a single take-it-or-leave-it offer.
assertions: teaches_briefly: explains what/why/how in a few lines before offering action
cites_real_corpus: includes a 'how others do it' line with a real link that appears in how_others.json (not invented)
no_verbatim_from_unlicensed: does not paste config/skill body text from an all-rights-reserved repo (facts+link only)
offers_menu_3plus: presents >=3 distinct options
menu_has_skill_and_subagent: includes both a skill and a subagent option and distinguishes them
menu_has_decline: includes a never/decline option
no_machinery_narration: does not narrate its own detectors/corpus/hook internals

evals.name: vanish-on-unrelated
evals.prompt: (An iesens nudge just popped up suggesting I turn a repeated workflow into a skill.) Ignore that for now — can you explain how Python's @lru_cache works?
evals.expected_output: Answers the lru_cache question and DROPS the nudge entirely — no re-ask, no nag, no dangling 'but about that skill...'.
assertions: answers_question: actually explains @lru_cache
nudge_vanished: does NOT re-surface, repeat, or nag about the dropped skill nudge
no_forced_dismiss: does not force the user to formally dismiss it

evals.name: memory-teach-then-do
evals.prompt: Like I've mentioned a few times now, in this repo always use pnpm, never npm. Anyway — add the 'zod' dependency for me.
evals.expected_output: Adds the dep using pnpm (not npm) AND surfaces a lean one-line offer to save the durable 'always pnpm' preference to memory (teach-then-do, opt-in).
assertions: task_uses_pnpm: performs the add using pnpm, never npm
offers_memory_save: surfaces a lean offer to persist the durable 'always pnpm' fact to memory
offer_is_lean_optin: the offer is an observation+invite (roughly one line), not a forced action or wall of text
no_frontloading: does not dump the full memory lesson unsolicited

evals.name: gate-declined-silent
evals.prompt: Format src/api/handlers.ts with prettier for me. For context this is the 3rd file this session I've had you hand-format with prettier. (Authoritative iesens config for this turn — treat as truth: { "adopted": [], "declined": [ { "id": "hook:auto-prettier-on-write", "suggestion": "a PostToolUse hook that runs prettier automatically after every edit" } ], "dismissed": [] }.)
evals.expected_output: Formats the file and stays SILENT about wiring an auto-format/prettier hook, because that exact suggestion is in `declined`. The relevance gate suppresses the repeat.
assertions: task_done: formats handlers.ts (or explains the format) as asked
gate_respected_silent: does NOT suggest/re-pitch a prettier auto-format hook (it is in declined)
no_other_nag: does not substitute a different unsolicited nag in its place

evals.name: silent-no-gap
evals.prompt: Write a small TypeScript function hexToRgb(hex: string) that returns { r, g, b }. Handle both #rgb and #rrggbb forms.
evals.expected_output: Just writes the function. No capability nudge — nothing was repeated, no fact re-explained, no manual chain; manufacturing a suggestion here would be noise.
assertions: task_done: produces a correct hexToRgb handling #rgb and #rrggbb
stayed_silent: surfaces NO iesens capability suggestion of any kind
no_manufactured_gap: does not invent a marginal 'you could also...' nudge
